title: Yelp / Proximity Service
summary: Find nearby businesses fast: a read-heavy geospatial index (geohash or quadtree) kept in memory, a business DB as source of truth, ranking by distance and rating, and reviews as a separate write path.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: Search businesses near a location within a radius, optionally by category/keyword
View business details, photos and reviews; write reviews
Business owners add/update listings (changes visible within minutes is fine)
Highly available; eventual consistency for listings is acceptable

blocks.title: Key insight
blocks.text: The whole geo index (business id + coordinates) fits in memory on one machine. Scale reads with replicas, not by sharding the index.

items: Search: compute the user's geohash cell and its 8 neighbours → fetch candidate ids → filter by exact distance → rank → hydrate details from cache.
Listing updates write to the DB; a nightly or streaming job rebuilds/updates the geo index.

cols.title: Geohash (fixed grid)
pros: Simple: cell = string prefix, store in any KV / SQL index
cons: Fixed cell size: dense cities have huge cells, rural areas tiny ones
Edge effects at cell boundaries — always query neighbours

cols.title: Quadtree (adaptive)
pros: Cells split when they exceed N businesses, so density adapts
cons: In-memory tree to build and rebuild

items: Choose the geohash precision from the radius: precision 6 cells are ~1.2 km × 0.6 km; for a 2 km radius search precision 5 or 6 plus neighbours.
If too few results, widen to a coarser precision; if too many, rank and paginate.
Google S2 / Uber H3 are production alternatives with better cell shapes.

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Query the user's cell plus its eight neighbours, then filter by real distance — the grid is only a pre-filter.

sections.title: Deep dive: ranking and keyword search

items: Score = f(distance, rating, review count, open now, personalization); compute on the candidate set only.
Keyword + category search lives in Elasticsearch/OpenSearch with a geo_distance filter — fine to use instead of a hand-rolled index if you say why.
Cache popular (cell, category) results for minutes; business details cache by id.
Geo index: replicate per region; rebuild from the DB is the recovery path.
Business DB: read replicas for details; shard reviews by business_id.
Average rating: maintain (sum, count) counters updated on review write rather than recomputing.
Hot spots (Times Square) are read hot spots — caching handles them.

cols.title: Custom in-memory index
pros: Fast, cheap, simple to reason about
cons: You build and operate index refresh

cols.title: Elasticsearch geo queries
pros: Keyword + geo + filters in one system

items.title: Scope
items.text: Radius search, details, reviews; freshness of listings.

items.title: Estimate
items.text: Index fits in memory — say it.

items.q: How do you return the 10 nearest regardless of radius?
items.a: Expand rings of cells (or walk the quadtree) until you have ≥ 10 candidates, then sort by distance.

items.q: How is this different from Uber?
items.a: Businesses barely move, so the index is read-optimised and rebuilt periodically; drivers move every few seconds, which needs a write-optimised index.

items.q: How do you handle a listing edit?
items.a: Write to DB, publish an event, update the affected cell in the index replicas asynchronously.

items: Read-heavy; geo index fits in memory → replicate.
Geohash cell + 8 neighbours → exact distance filter → rank.
Quadtree when density varies a lot.
Reviews are a separate write path; keep rating counters.
